newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Motorola busy as stock rallies.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Motorola busy as stock rallies.

text.p: Call options on Motorola Inc were busy Wednesday as the stock rallied on heavy volume after the company posted better-than-expected second quarter earnings late Tuesday.
Motorola ended up 3-1/2 at 86 on more than nine million shares in consolidated activity. The stock reached 87 intraday.

Todd Salamone, an analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said Motorola's recent options activity suggested investors were still fairly skeptical on the stock despite its recent strong run.
"A lot of the call volume has not translated into open interest, indicating two-way paper," he said. "That means that there are people that are skeptical giving up on it."
He added that some investors were adding out-of-the-money puts, another sign of bearishness.
As long as out-of-the-money call accumulation does not begin to show up, the stock should have upside potential, Salamone said.
"The momentum's there," he added.
Gregory Nie at EVEREN Securities recommended taking some profits because the stock has gotten extended short term.
Motorola has been rallying steadily since late April when it bottomed off the 55 region. Its latest breakout came in late June when it gapped from around 70 to the 72 zone.

"On a trading basis, take the short term-oriented money, the speculative money out with every intention of buying it back," Nie said. "I am looking for some consolidation or mild dose of well earned profit-taking as an opportunity to buy that trading half back."
He added that if any consolidation holds the low 70 area or better, the stock would have an upside target of around 115.
"If that consolidation is contained to the low 70's or higher, it's going to lend credibility to an eventual target--with a heavy emphasis on eventual -- of 115 or better," he said.

Nie explained that such a contained pullback would suggest the stock has completed a long term basing pattern, a head and shoulders-type bottom with a neckline at 82 that would produce the 115 target.
On the options side, Salamone said the trading pattern could turn any time, but that through Tuesday, skepticism remained solid.
The heaviest option activity Wednesday was in the in-the-money July 80 call, which traded more than 8,100 contracts, and the in-the-money August 85 call, which traded about 3,160.
Salamone said those trades were not a concern.

"It's the out-of-the-money activity that I like to look at," he explained. The most active out-of-the-money Motorola call was the January 90, which traded 860 contracts. The August 90 call traded 835.
"As soon as we see that out-of-the-money call accumulation begin to set in, it could be near the top," he said.
